sentences.text: Bayannurosaurus was a large iguanodontian dinosaur that could reach a total body length of up to 9 meters, though its skull measured only 80 cm in length.
Scientists know this animal only from a nearly complete, partially articulated holotype skeleton that preserves the entire tail.
A joint expedition exploring the Chulumiao locality in Bayannur, China, took place in the summer of 2013, leading to the description of Bayannurosaurus in 2018 by the paleontologist Xu Xing.

Bayannurosaurus is classified as an intermediate form of Ankylopollexia, showing features transitional between earlier members and hadrosauriforms. Researchers suggest that Bayannurosaurus and Lanzhousaurus resulted from allopatric speciation in Asia, separate from the immigration events linked to the origins of Hadrosauroidea.
Bayannurosaurus lived approximately 124 million years ago during the Berriasian stage of the early Cretaceous in what is now Asia, specifically within the Bayin-Gobi Formation.
